approachQuestion.prompt:
One-Way Shelf

Two strings start and goal of equal length n describe shelf cells: L is a left-moving token, R is a right-moving token, and _ is empty. One legal move swaps L with the immediately preceding _ (L moves one cell left), or swaps R with the immediately following _ (R moves one cell right). Tokens cannot pass through one another. Return whether start can become goal by zero or more legal moves. Inputs are read-only.

Constraints: 0 <= n <= 200000; the alphabet is exactly L,R,_.

Example 1: start="_L__R_", goal="L____R" -> true.
Example 2: start="R_L_", goal="_LR_" -> false (token order would change).
Example 3: start="L_", goal="_L" -> false (L cannot move right).
constraints: Choose the most efficient valid approach for the entire stated input domain; accept equivalent optimal variants.

options.text: Scan each string past empty cells to align its next token. Require identical token types. For L require its start index to be at least its goal index; for R require its start index to be at most its goal index. Accept only if both scans exhaust together.
options.feedback: Moves preserve token order and obey those inequalities. Conversely, ordered tokens satisfying their directional constraints can be moved through available gaps without crossing.

options.text: Build each string's ordered list of (token,index) records. Compare types and the same directional index inequalities for corresponding records.
options.feedback: These are the right conditions, but materializing all token records can be replaced by simultaneous scans.

options.text: Remove _ from both strings and accept exactly when the resulting token strings are equal.
options.feedback: For start="L_" and goal="_L", token order matches but the required rightward L move is forbidden.

options.text: For each token type independently, pair its occurrences in left-to-right order and check the directional index inequalities, without checking the combined order of L and R tokens.
options.feedback: For start="R_L" and goal="L_R", R can appear to move right and L left, but they would have to cross, which legal moves cannot do.

feedback.reason: Align nonempty tokens while enforcing order and one-sided position constraints; matching a subsequence alone is insufficient.
details: Skip underscores independently in start and goal to find corresponding tokens. Reject different token types. Reject an L whose start position is left of its goal position, or an R whose start position is right of its goal position. Continue until both strings are exhausted; reject if only one still has tokens.

Tokens cannot pass each other, so their nonblank order must agree. L can only end at its start or farther left; R can only end at its start or farther right. These directional inequalities avoid simulating individual moves.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method revealed after question 1, choose its tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Use a word-RAM model with constant-time indexed access and signed 64-bit arithmetic. Include all temporary buffers, input copies, and call frames; exclude supplied input and returned output. n is common string length. The fixed scan is iterative and has no string filtering copies, token arrays, recursion, hashing, or amortized operations.
constraints: Analyze this fixed method regardless of your answer to question 1; choose the tightest pair.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Two positional scans decide feasibility without storing move sequences.
details: Each scan passes at most n characters. Identical long arrangements require checking every character, giving linear worst-case time. Only indices and current token values are stored; the algorithm decides feasibility without simulating moves.

Use a word-RAM model with constant-time indexed access and signed 64-bit arithmetic. Include all temporary buffers, input copies, and call frames; exclude supplied input and returned output. n is common string length. The fixed scan is iterative and has no string filtering copies, token arrays, recursion, hashing, or amortized operations.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This adds an input-sized buffer absent from the fixed method.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This counts repeated full scans that the fixed method does not perform.
“O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The fixed method does not perform sorting or independent binary searches.
